newsitem.title: USA: CME to temporarily delist June 1998 live cattle.
newsitem.headline: CME to temporarily delist June 1998 live cattle.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange, in an executive report, said it has received Commodity Futures Trading Commission approval to temporarily delist the June 1998 live cattle contract.
The delisting was sought in anticipation of CFTC's approval of amendments to live cattle contracts submitted on January 6.

One of those changes is to increase the position limit on the spot month to 600 contracts from 300 contracts until the last five days of trading when position limits would then go down to 300 contracts.
Others include changing the last trading day to the last day of the month and a host of changes to premiums and discounts on delivery cattle.
Also, U.S. Department of Agriculture reports would be used instead of the current set 20 to 25 percent charge for being out of the delivery weight range, a CME spokesman said.

Upon CFTC approval of these amendments, the June 1998 contract would be immediately re-listed for trading. This would restore the normal roster of seven concurrently-listed Live Cattle contract months, CME added.
